Key takeaways The days between checkout and the first carrier scan are when holiday gift buyers worry most, and default platform emails say nothing during them. Five pre-ship messages close the gap: a dated confirmation, a fulfillment delay alert, "ready to ship" at label creation, the shipping confirmation at first scan, and carrier pickup delay notices. Manual catch-all emails at peak create tickets, while per-order triggers from your fulfillment and carrier data keep a small team out of the queue. UK gifting retailer Fortnum & Mason cut WISMO queries 50% with Narvar Track and Notify. It is December 14. A shopper orders a personalized photo book for her mother, with a delivery date two days before Christmas. The order confirmation arrives within a minute. Then nothing for three days. Inside the operation, the book is being printed, bound, packed, and labeled. On the shopper's phone, nothing has changed since checkout. By the third morning she has clicked the tracking link twice, found a label with no scans, and opened a chat to ask whether the gift will make it. That chat is the cheap outcome. The expensive one is the shopper who never asks, watches the gift land on December 27, and spends her January budget somewhere else. A holiday order comes with a date the shopper can't move Most orders carry an expectation. A holiday order carries a deadline, and the shopper measures your brand against it. In Delivering the 2026 Holiday Shopping Season from Narvar and eTail Insights, 68% of US shoppers rate on-time delivery "very important," and 66% of retailers rank it as a top-three peak challenge. Gifts are the sharpest case because two people are involved. The buyer carries the worry while the recipient gets the box, so every day without an update lands on the person who paid. For a Growth-stage retailer, the commercial math is direct. A late gift costs you a refund or a reship in December and a repeat customer in the new year. Our research found that 44% of shoppers say order and delivery notifications would make them buy from a retailer again. The longest silence happens before the first carrier scan Carrier tracking starts when a carrier scans the package. Everything before that scan is invisible to the shopper unless you tell them about it: picking, packing, production for made-to-order items, label creation, and the wait for pickup. A personalized-gifts retailer we work with calls this stretch a three-day black box, and it is where holiday anxiety peaks. The shopper has paid, the clock is running, and the most recent message they have is a receipt. The standard platform message set misses this window. Shopify and most commerce platforms send an order confirmation, then shipped and delivered. Shoppers in that gap check the tracking page, see "label created" with no movement, and conclude something is wrong. In Narvar's work with retailers, we plan around a shopper who expects to hear from you about every two days. Three days of silence breaks that expectation before the box ever leaves the building. Get the complete shopper data. See how 1,348 US shoppers plan to buy, and what they expect after checkout, Download the report . Five timed messages that cover the pre-ship window The goal is one message at each point where the shopper's question changes. Here is the sequence we recommend for holiday and deadline orders, built on the pre-shipment events in Narvar Notify . 1. At checkout, confirm the date and say what happens next. The order confirmation is the only message most shoppers are guaranteed to read. Use it to restate the delivery date and describe the steps ahead. For made-to-order gifts, name the production step and how long it takes, so day two without a shipping email reads as normal. 2. When fulfillment slips, say so before the shopper notices. A fulfillment delay or backorder message fires when your order data shows an item running behind. Send it the moment the slip happens, and tell the shopper whether the holiday date still holds. A shopper who hears about a one-day slip on day two stays calm. A shopper who discovers it on day five opens a ticket. 3. At label creation, call it "ready to ship." A label means the package is packed and waiting for the carrier. Telling the shopper it has shipped sends them to a tracking page with no scans. A "ready to ship" message gives them progress without the false alarm. 4. At the first carrier scan, send the shipping confirmation. Holding the shipping email until the carrier scans the box is our top recommendation for cutting WISMO ("where is my order") contacts. The tracking link works the first time the shopper clicks it, and the next message they get comes from a package that is moving. 5. If the carrier hasn't picked up, send a pickup delay notice, then a second one. A missed pickup leaves the package sitting with a label and no scan. Notify supports a carrier pickup delay sequence, with a first notice on day two and a follow-up on day five if the package still hasn't moved. Each one tells the shopper you are watching the order, which is the reassurance they wanted from a support chat. A small team can't send these by hand in December Every one of those messages depends on timing. The fulfillment delay has to go out when the slip happens, and the shipping confirmation when the scan arrives. A small ecommerce team trying to cover this manually ends up exporting a list of aging orders each morning and emailing everyone on it. That approach backfires at holiday volume. Broad catch-all emails reach shoppers whose orders are fine, raise questions they weren't asking, and push ticket counts up during the weeks you can least absorb them. The personalized-gifts retailer above described exactly this: blanket inquiry emails at Christmas that created noise and spiked support volume. blogs.content: Klaviyo’s commerce data and AI agent strengths Generated by Klaviyo AI Klaviyo was named a Challenger in its first evaluation in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Multichannel Marketing Hubs. The post explains its commerce-focused customer profiles, the distinct roles of Customer Agent and Composer, and how Klaviyo Data Platform supports personalized journeys. Commerce focus: Klaviyo combines transaction histories, browsing activity, campaign responses, and product reviews into profiles used across email, SMS, push, and web. Customer conversations: Customer Agent handles service and sales conversations within brand-defined guardrails, feeding customer preferences and intent signals back into profiles. Campaign support: Composer identifies marketing opportunities and builds omnichannel campaigns, with explicit human approval required before launch. Sign up Get a demo Show AI generated summary Klaviyo has been recognized in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Multichannel Marketing Hubs, named a Challenger in our first year in the evaluation. Gartner named Klaviyo a Challenger, and customers agree: Klaviyo is rated 4.7/5 on Gartner Peer Insights for Multichannel Marketing Hubs. What Gartner credited us for is exactly what we know large consumer brands are asking for right now: a platform built for commerce, AI agents that do real work across your business, and a data platform that keeps those agents grounded in what your customers are actually doing. We aren't here to protect legacy software paradigms or maintain the status quo. We're building what consumer brands need to scale profitably. Built for retail and ecommerce Gartner recognized Klaviyo as a commerce-centered marketing platform, noting that brands can bring transaction histories, on-site browsing, campaign responses, and product reviews into individual profiles, then activate those profiles across email, SMS, push, and web using built-in predictive analytics. That focus is intentional. We built Klaviyo around the data commerce runs on: what people browse, what they buy, and what brings them back. It's helped consumer brands drive over $300 billion in attributed value. For large retail and ecommerce brands, that means Klaviyo already speaks your language on day one, and houses all relevant consumer data necessary for your team to create unparalleled consumer experiences that make your brand stand out. Two AI agents, working across your entire business Gartner also named Klaviyo's AI agents, Customer Agent and Composer , a strength. Gartner noted that Composer requires explicit human approval before anything launches, while Customer Agent resolves two-way service and sales conversations on its own, inside guardrails your brand sets. In the companion 2026 Gartner® Critical Capabilities for Multichannel Marketing Hubs, our strongest use cases were conversational and agent-augmented marketing, and omnichannel workflow innovation. Gartner pointed to Customer Agent handling both service and merchandising as one agent: it answers product questions, adds items to the cart, and applies promotion rules right in the conversation. What a shopper shares here then becomes reusable audience data, and that context carries over when a conversation moves to a live agent. We know that managing millions of individual customer relationships across channels is a monumental task. That’s why we split the work between two agents built on one connected customer profile: one that talks directly to shoppers, and one that runs campaigns alongside your marketing team. Neither agent works in isolation, so nothing gets stranded in one channel nor impacts your customer's brand experience. Customer Agent talks to your customers Customer Agent handles two-way customer conversations, delivering 24/7 service that also drives real-time sales. Resolves support issues and closes sales in the same conversation: Operates as an autonomous brand expert across email, web chat, text, and WhatsApp. It answers complex product questions, guides purchases, and resolves issues without hold times or transfers. Continuous profile enrichment: Every conversation automatically enriches the underlying customer profile. Interactions don't stay trapped in support logs. Customer preferences, sizing notes, and intent signals immediately feed back into future marketing flows, discount decisions, and channel targeting. New skills, described in plain language: With Agent Builder, your team describes what you want Customer Agent to do, and Klaviyo AI builds the skill. Gartner noted that Agent Builder also tests and ships each skill and logs every change in an audit trail, so your marketers (not your engineers) stay in control of what the agent can do. Global and multilingual: Supports over 100 languages with automatic regional locale, pricing, and catalog detection to serve international audiences natively. Composer works alongside your marketing team Composer , Klaviyo's AI marketing agent, works like an expert marketer embedded in your team's day-to-day. Proactive campaign building: Composer continuously audits marketing performance and identifies revenue opportunities and churn risks. By automating multi-location coordination and routine campaign builds, brands like Scheels are saving upwards of 32 hours per week on manual marketing work. Real-time data processing Processes over 4 billion signals daily across 9+ billion profiles, triggering single-customer flows in milliseconds. Direct SQL & MCP access Grants complete data access through KSQL and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, letting custom agents and external tools query Klaviyo data seamlessly. The team used Klaviyo's MCP server and Claude to analyze which skin concerns and customer traits correlated with engagement on two recent product launches, turning that signal into sharper targeting for future launches. Across more than 4 million active customer profiles and over 100 million events processed annually, that data-to-action loop has driven 21% year-over-year growth in CRM revenue . blogs.author: Tracey Wallace
blogs.content: Turning automated analytics into weekly strategy Generated by Klaviyo AI Dagne Dover centralized its marketing data and automated reporting with Claude and Klaviyo’s MCP server, saving about six hours each Monday. The post explains how integrated data, scheduled analysis, and human validation help the team spend less time gathering numbers and more time planning. Centralized data: Dubay connected Klaviyo, Shopify, and Google Sheets data through Claude and Klaviyo’s MCP server to ask performance questions in plain language. Scheduled reporting: Daily analysis delivered through Slack replaced manual reporting work and freed about six hours each Monday for strategy. Human validation: Clean source data and Dubay’s review of every report help catch errors before findings reach the wider company. Clearer creative briefs: Dubay tests prompts in Composer to visualize email concepts and refine briefs before handing them to designers. Integrated tools first: Dubay recommends integrating existing tools and checking which data sources MCP connectors can access before starting AI reporting. Sign up Get a demo Show AI generated summary Dagne Dover ’s functional bags are built to keep everything organized and within reach. Caitlin Dubay , director of marketing, wanted the same for the brand’s data. Dubay runs marketing and analytics for the 50-person brand where everyone owns a piece of the revenue. She was previously working with a decentralized set-up many marketers will recognize: 60% of marketing teams have 6–15 tools in their tech stack, according to Klaviyo’s 2025 State of B2C Marketing Report . Recently, Dubay consolidated all of Dagne Dover’s data sources to one place, so she can get answers on marketing performance via AI conversations rather than solely relying on reports. In our latest episode of Klaviyo Originals , Dubay explains how she uses AI to reclaim time and get performance data she can act on right away. The first step: centralizing data with an MCP server With Claude and Klaviyo’s MCP server , Dubay pulled Dagne Dover’s Klaviyo data , Shopify data, and revenue plans and marketing calendar in Google Sheets into one place. "We've basically brought in all of our data sources into our own version of a data warehouse, and now we're able to have almost human-like, analyst-level conversations with AI,” Dubay says. MCP is an open protocol that helps AI models securely interface with data sources and tools. This is what makes it possible for marketers like Dubay to interact with their data warehouse analytics through Claude and get answers about performance in plain language. But for that to work, all customer and performance data need to be centralized at the source. An LLM can only answer questions about the performance data that’s visible to it, which is why Dubay’s initial centralization efforts were so crucial to her success. Reclaiming report Mondays: “Instead of gathering data, we can come up with our weekly game plan” Dubay’s analysis runs on its own schedule, so she doesn’t need to manually build reports. "The AI workflow is based on a trigger," Dubay says. "I have schedules in place, so that each morning it runs the analysis and then Slacks me, as if I had a data analyst on my team telling me exactly what happened the day before." These conversations keep Dubay in the loop, and now her job is to check the output and make it useful for everyone else. "From there, I’m reviewing that and making sure it makes sense, and translating it in a way that’s valuable for our team," she explains. Before the switch, Dubay needed most of Monday to open 10 tabs and manually pull data for the team's weekly report, which she presented at a 4 p.m. meeting. Automating that process gave her back about 6 hours each Monday. The meeting now happens at 10 a.m. "It really gives us all of Monday back,” Dubay says. “Instead of gathering data, we can come up with our game plan for the week and be strategic.” The extra time also changed how the team works together. "We work less in silos," Dubay points out. “So instead of everyone on Monday morning crunching the numbers for the channels they own, we're all able to come together and have a team discussion about the marketing at Dagne Dover as a whole." Humans in the loop: "AI is only as good as its inputs" Most marketers have seen AI deliver an answer that turns out to be wrong. Dubay guards against that with clean inputs and a final human review. "There's a lot of fine-tuning that goes into it, and I think the AI is only going to be as good as its inputs," Dubay says. "So, the first step is making sure you have clean sources, and that the data itself is clean to begin with." Checking inputs doesn’t catch everything, though. Sometimes a report comes back with a number that doesn’t add up. That’s why every report goes to Dubay before it goes to anyone else. "I would say we’re about 95% there, but I think that’s where a human is super important,” Dubay says. “I’ll read through it first before I distribute it anywhere in the company, and do some of those data validation checks.” How Dagne Dover turns data into marketing decisions With automated reporting, Dubay’s team spends more of the week acting on their data. “We always want to have brand at the forefront and remain creative,” Dubay says. “But at the same time, we always look to the data to support our theories that our brains are coming up with.” The same habit shapes how Dagne Dover is preparing for shoppers who use AI. To learn how customers describe their needs, the brand launched an AI customer agent on their website. “I think we see humans being a little bit more brutally honest when they don't see the person behind the screen,” Dubay says. "I'm really excited to see how people interact with it, because our theory is that customers will tell us exactly what they need.” Recent Klaviyo research supports that theory: 78% of consumers include emotional or personal context at least some of the time when using AI, according to Klaviyo's 2026 AI Consumer Trends Report . Dubay is also making sure Dagne Dover shows up in AI search results outside the brand’s owned channels. For AI shopping visibility, she mentions the importance of press, "making sure you're mentioned in those top bags for back-to-school roundups," as well as community threads like Reddit, customer reviews, and product page metadata that matches how customers describe their needs. From analyzing performance to briefing the next campaign As an analytics expert, “sometimes it’s really hard for me, as a non-creative, to thoughtfully communicate what I’m asking them for,” Dubay points out. “If you asked me to put together any design, it would never get approved.” So, she tests her briefs in Composer , Klaviyo’s built-in AI marketing agent, before passing them to her creative team. "I put my prompt into Composer, and have it build the email for me,” she explains. “I can start to visualize what the outcome of my words is going to look like, and get it to a place that I feel good about, so I can pass it over to a digital designer." How lean teams can get started with AI reporting For lean teams that want to try AI marketing analytics, Dubay’s advice is to start with the tools already in their tech stack. Specifically, she advises teams to: Consolidate and integrate your tech stack before you begin. "Get your tech stack as integrated as you can,” she suggests. Learn from others. "I’ll look up TikToks on how to optimize this specific thing within Claude,” she says. “There's a wealth of information out there.” Audit MCP servers against data sources. "Look at the connectors, then see out of your tech stack what you can connect to, and what you can't," she recommends. With easier access to Dagne Dover’s data, Dubay and her team can spend less time with spreadsheets and more time with strategy. Tracey Wallace Tracey is the director of content strategy at Klaviyo.
